scope: Bounded review queries; no new literature sweep or new primary evidence registration

answers.resolution: Recovered labelled eligibility list: 16 CORINE 2018 classes covering pasture, grassland, selected crops, shrubland and forest. Section 2.1 excludes other classes from this EU Mediterranean analysis; this is a source eligibility mask, not 16 equally high suitability scores. MaxEnt later assigns suitability. Keep regional mask distinct from a global WorldCover crosswalk and from proof of grazing.

The 61.3% is MaxEnt permutation importance, not a class score or default MCDA weight. Linked to the separate 16-class CORINE eligibility record. Relative to equal importance among the source model’s 14 predictors, 61.3% is 8.58 times the mean if using the conventional 100%-total permutation scale. This comparison is diagnostic only; no importance was invented for the other predictors.

Yes. Table 2 verifies annual mean temperature (WorldClim BIO1) as one of 14 MaxEnt predictors. It counts once as a model-used variable even without cutoffs. No monotonic direction, temperature optimum or weight is stated here; those remain unknown. Duplicate records from this paper cannot add another temperature vote.

References are useful. Ref 125 directly reports a positive association between specialized silvopastoral training and adoption in Colombia; ref 110 is a review/framework, and ref 126 studies Colombian adoption. Added exact references and links. Kiziridis is secondary evidence here, not its own training experiment. Retain operational guidance; originals need registered, claim-specific extraction before they become additional independent votes.

Agreed. Over 85% describes inherited plots in the study sample, not a tenure threshold or evidence that inheritance guarantees security. Restored the truncated sentence, including the warning that women’s plots could still face tenure issues which these data could not assess. Removed the inferred suitability direction; retained contextual implementation evidence.

Corrected variable to farm asset ownership/index, not credit access. The paper’s own Table 2 reports a positive association with fertilizer-tree adoption. This is a wealth/equipment proxy, not evidence of borrowing access and not a causal credit effect. New ontology term remains pending with no spatial dataset binding.

This finding is from Coulibaly’s own analysis: section 5.1 and Table 2 list agroforestry training as an adoption predictor. The following Franzel et al. (2001) citation is corroborating discussion, not the origin of the reported result. Retain Coulibaly as one source; describe a positive association, not experimentally proven causation.

Correct: the general labour-burden statement cites reference 22, Barrett, Place and Aboud (eds., 2002), Natural Resources Management in African Agriculture. Reference 13 supports the distinct Tephrosia comparison. Added explicit source lineage; this is secondary qualitative implementation evidence, not a measured labour coefficient from Snapp’s experiment.

Agreed. The claim is that maize–Tephrosia has relatively modest labour requirements compared with other agroforestry systems. It does not establish a positive labour-availability response. Removed the positive direction and retained a qualitative practice comparison linked to Snapp et al. (2002), reference 13. No numeric labour reduction or general suitability curve inferred.

Operational risk and next steps, not core T4. The source cites reference 7 as Pham et al. (2019), Factors influencing the adoption of agroforestry and evergreen agriculture in Vietnam uplands. Its printed DOI returned no Crossref record during this check. Citation is recorded as reported, not verified; original-source identity remains unresolved. Retain the attributed qualitative claim, with no independent original-paper vote or numeric calibration.

Bulk density is now explicitly recorded as model use. Page 6 lists it as an input and Table 1 gives a published weight of 0.064 (6.4%). This model ranks tree-species groups, so the vote stays in the species-specific lane; it does not increase general agroforestry agreement. No monotonic response is supplied by this paragraph. Historical soildrain ID remains stable; variable is soil_bulk_density.

Rainfall is already the canonical variable annual_precipitation. Added explicit name and units inside the displayed values too. The 400–800 mm/year interval describes greatest observed spread of regreening; the source explicitly allows regreening below 400 mm/year. Retained as observed spread/growth context, not a hard rainfall gate or an upper suitability limit.

The two passages repeat one source-level association: tree cover and biomass carbon tend to be higher in humid regions. Linked the second record to the first for deduplication; its existing dropped state is unchanged. This is observed distribution, not a calibrated suitability response. Removed the generic negative aridity-index direction because numerical sign depends on the chosen index definition. Source ID says 2014, but cached publication is Scientific Reports 2016, 6:29987; stable ID retained.

Table 2 explicitly gates silvopasture to pasture/grassland, with grazing animals in the practice definition. Added source dataset and class wording. The associated code selects CDL class 176 and removes ESA WorldCover tree class 10. This regional tool therefore targets introducing silvopasture on open pasture, not every existing wooded grazing system. A grassland label alone still does not confirm local grazing; no global crosswalk inferred.

Linked the statement to all four references: Thiesmeier & Zander (2023), Lehmann et al. (2020), Giannitsopoulos et al. (2020), and Kay et al. (2019). The statement concerns profitability under policies/incentives, not a credit threshold or a structural T4 condition. Retain as secondary operational/implementation guidance. The four originals are not automatically four independent votes and require claim-specific checking before direct extraction.

Reference 50 is Mercer, Frey & Cubbage (2014), Economics of agroforestry, Handbook of Forest Resource Economics, pp204–225. Added that lineage. Castle then uses hired/unpaid workers per operation as its own county-level labour-availability indicator, with an expected positive effect on social acceptability. Distinguish the borrowed rationale from Castle’s model input; neither is a measured universal labour threshold.

Indirect financial support is broader than access to credit. The ontology label already covers rural finance/credit/project support; retained that broad group and explicitly marked the source concept as indirect programme support, with credit access not measured. This passage describes a proposed intervention pathway, not an isolated causal estimate or a numeric finance suitability rule.

Resolved from the full calculation: alley-cropping weights are 5, 5, 5, 3 and 1, then the last two are halved to 1.5 and 0.5. Total is 17. Each weight 5 therefore contributes 29.41% of the environmental-priority subscore, or 1.47 times the five-input average. This is an environmental-benefit priority, not structural suitability or the final model weight. Record remains quarantined from T4; no reapproval requested for the denominator arithmetic.

Code masks are now explicit by practice, and checked against the Earth Engine CDL dictionary. Alley cropping selects the crop predicate OR pasture 176, excluding WorldCover tree class 10; silvopasture selects pasture 176 alone with that exclusion. The crop comment is misleading: its predicate also accepts Background 0, hay, switchgrass, fallow/idle land and berry crops. Background may be masked in the input; no affected area was measured. Saved all selected named codes in the audit. Do not reuse this numeric predicate as a global mask; exact 2022 dictionary and pixel-mask behavior remain checks before adoption.
